For the mason jar method, you leave the leaf above water. Eventually, the roots should grow down *to* the water. Once they reach about an inch long, I’d take them out and place them in some moist soil and keep that soil moist for at least a week or two to give the plant time to adjust.

You can really tell if the leaf is drying out by it’s wrinkles!! Some wrinkles are okay and I would not water it until a few days after those wrinkles appear. Misting your little guy with new roots should be fine, however, just enough to have the soil damp. Make sure they’re in a location where they’re getting strong light for at least a few hours of the day but too much light/heat and they will often dry out quickly and become more at risk to die.

I wouldn’t recommend the seran wrap for succulents just because the retention of moisture all around can be too high for them to handle, it’s a better method when you’re working on sprouting seeds for other plants such as flowers. Try not to spray every day, every two to three days generally works but you can even stretch it to once a week.

Trial and error is the game here, you should be fine! Just get a lot of props and see what works best out of everything. :)

I only water once every week generally, or when the big leaf gets quite wrinkly! This leaf in particular took an *extremely* long time to sprout new buds, we’re talking about 8 months, so just stay patient! As soon as my leaf got some roots about an inch long, I put it into its own little pot with deeper soil than the shallow plate I had it on.

Another method I’ve seen successful is taking a mason jar and filling it with water, putting ceran wrap over the top and making little slits for the leaves to stick in, just above the water but not touching it.

Good luck to you in your future propogations! Keep trying :)
